qualifyingPathways: Meteorological, soil, and/or hydrologic conditions may lead to flooding
Meteorological, soil, hydrologic, and/or burn-area conditions may lead to debris flows
A dam or levee may fail and threaten life or property, but failure is not imminent

operationalSignalsToTest.ndfdQpf: Every grid cell intersecting each forecast-zone polygon
operationalSignalsToTest.flashFloodGuidance: Local RFC 1-, 3-, and 6-hour guidance where available
operationalSignalsToTest.riverForecasts: Forecast flood-stage exceedance for river-driven watches
operationalSignalsToTest.damLevee: Requires authoritative incident information; cannot be inferred from QPF

requiredInputs: Exact active NWS Flood Watch for the forecast zone and valid period
Fresh zone-wide NDFD QPF during that period
Overlapping WPC Excessive Rainfall Outlook Marginal Risk or higher
excludedCauses: rain-on-snow flooding without independently supported rainfall forcing
river flooding without independently supported rainfall forcing

PQR.note: Portland impact guidance varies by season and duration; examples include winter 0.25 inch/hour for 3-4 hours or 0.5 inch/hour for 2 hours, with separate burn-scar debris-flow handling.

MKX.note: Rapidly developing, life-threatening flooding possible from heavy rain or dam/levee failure; typical lead time 6-48 hours.

BOX.note: At least a 50% chance of flooding/debris-flow conditions, normally within 48 hours; longer lead is permitted when appropriate.

HFO.note: Flood Watches may be issued up to 48 hours before expected flash flooding.

researchQuestions: How often does the WPC Marginal-or-higher gate miss rainfall-driven Flood Watches?
How much does adding RFC flash-flood guidance improve office and zone matching?
Should any-point QPF be paired with an areal or basin probability signal to avoid isolated-grid false alarms?
How should dam, levee, burn-scar, snowmelt, and ice-jam watches fail closed?
notes: WPC ERO is guidance, not a mandatory national prerequisite for a Flood Watch.
No single nationwide rainfall-total threshold is supported by NWS criteria.
This file is not consumed by live automation.
